heroData.title: EOR & PEO Services in Chile
heroData.subtitle: Compliant Hiring and Labor Leasing in the Southern Cone
heroData.description: Navigate the complex 2025 Chilean Labor Code transition with our local EOR infrastructure. We manage the phased reduction to a 40-hour work week, mandatory 25% 'Legal Gratification' bonuses, and integrated social security contributions via Previred.
heroData.bestFor: Companies looking to hire Chilean talent without a local entity while ensuring 100% compliance with evolving work-hour laws.

steps.title: Employment Contract Execution
steps.description: Drafting contracts in Spanish (mandatory) within 15 days of the start date. Contracts must specify job duties, schedule (transitioning to 40h), and the 'gratificación legal' method selected (Art. 47 or Art. 50).

steps.title: Social Security Registration (Previred)
steps.description: Mapping the employee to their respective AFP (Pension) and Fonasa/Isapre (Health). In Chile, the employer manages the withholding and payment through the Previred portal by the 13th of each month.

steps.title: Mandatory Life and Accident Insurance
steps.description: Registering with an 'Mutual de Seguridad' for work-related accident insurance. Employer contribution varies between 0.90% and 3.4% based on the company's risk profile.

steps.title: Digital Folder Setup
steps.description: Creating a digital employee record on the DT (Dirección del Trabajo) website. Electronic signatures for contracts and annexes are standard and legally binding in 2025.

steps.title: Equipment and Home-Office Stipends
steps.description: Arranging delivery of hardware and setting up non-taxable 'asignación de movilización' (commuter) and 'colación' (meal) allowances, which are standard in Chilean pay structures.

items.title: 40-Hour Week Transition
items.text: Chile is progressively reducing the work week from 45 to 40 hours. Ensure your EOR partner is updated on the latest reduction schedule (currently 44h in 2024, 42h in 2026, 40h in 2028).

items.title: Legal Gratification (Bonus)
items.text: Employers must pay 25% of the worker's monthly salary as a bonus, capped at 4.75 minimum wages annually, or share 30% of profits. Most EORs use the monthly 25% cap method.

items.title: Notice Periods and Severance
items.text: Termination requires 30 days' notice or payment in lieu. Severance (Indemnización por años de servicio) is 1 month per year worked, capped at 11 years for contracts post-1981.

items.title: Unemployment Insurance (AFC)
items.text: For indefinite contracts, the employer must contribute 2.4% of the taxable salary to the AFC. Fixed-term contracts require a 3% employer contribution.

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors through an EOR in Chile?
faqs.answer: EOR is for employment. For contractors (independent workers), you use 'Boletas de Honorarios'. However, misclassification is a high risk in Chile; EOR provides the safest compliant path for long-term roles.

faqs.question: What are 'Haberes No Imponibles'?
faqs.answer: These are non-taxable allowances like 'Colación' (meals) and 'Movilización' (transport). They should be reasonable and proportionate to the salary to avoid reclassification as taxable income.

faqs.question: How do public holidays work?
faqs.answer: Chile has approximately 16 public holidays. If a holiday falls on a weekend, it is rarely moved. Some are 'Irrenunciables' (Mandatory), where most retail businesses must close.

faqs.question: Is insurance mandatory for remote workers?
faqs.answer: Yes, Law 21.220 (Telework Law) mandates that employers provide all tools and materials. Employers must also ensure safety assessments are conducted for the home office.

items.title: Communication Style
items.text: Chileans tend to be polite and indirect. Building trust is essential before deep business collaboration.

items.title: The 'Huasco' Concept
items.text: Punctuality is expected in professional settings in Santiago, though some flexibility exists in more social contexts.

items.title: Hierarchical Structure
items.text: Chilean companies often maintain a clear hierarchy. Decisions usually come from the top down.

steps.title: Inputs and Variable Data Collection
steps.description: Gathering overtime hours (paid at 50% surcharge), sick leave certificates (Licencias Médicas), and variable bonuses before the 20th of the month.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Computation
steps.description: Calculating statutory deductions: ~7% for Health, ~10% for AFP, and the Unemployment fund (AFC). Applying the progressive Income Tax (Impuesto de Segunda Categoría).

steps.title: Previred Filing
steps.description: Generating the consolidated monthly report for all social security institutions. Payments must be remitted via Previred by the 10th (electronic) or 13th (if paying later) of the following month.

steps.title: Payroll Distribution (CLP)
steps.description: Executing bank transfers to local Chilean banks (Banco de Chile, Santander, BCI) in CLP. Payments are usually made on the last working day of the month.

steps.title: Annual Tax Declarations
steps.description: Preparing the 'Declaración Jurada 1887' (Annual Payroll Tax Return) submitted to the SII (Internal Revenue Service) every March.

items.title: Income Tax Brackets (UTM)
items.text: Tax brackets are calculated in UTM (Monthly Tax Unit). The exemption limit is roughly 13.5 UTM (~$800 USD) monthly. Rates scale up to 40%.

items.title: The 'Previred' Ecosystem
items.text: Previred is the centralized hub for all social security payments. Failure to pay on time triggers heavy dynamic interest charges and penalties.

items.title: Sick Leave Management
items.text: For leaves shorter than 11 days, the first 3 days are unpaid by the state/Isapre. Employers often cover this in competitive benefit packages.

items.title: July 2025 Minimum Wage
items.text: The minimum wage is set to reach 500,000 CLP net. Ensure all lower-tier salary bands are adjusted to meet this statutory floor.

faqs.question: What is the UF and how does it affect payroll?
faqs.answer: The 'Unidad de Fomento' (UF) is an inflation-indexed unit. Maximum taxable caps for social security are set in UF and change daily. As of early 2025, the cap is approximately 84.3 UF.

faqs.question: Are 13th-month salaries mandatory in Chile?
faqs.answer: No, they are not mandatory. However, 'Aguinaldos' (bonuses) for Independence Day (Sept 18) and Christmas are very common and often expected by employees.

faqs.question: How are overtime hours calculated?
faqs.answer: Overtime is any time worked beyond the agreed weekly hours. They are paid with a 50% surcharge on the hourly base salary and must be agreed upon in writing for max 2 hours per day.

faqs.question: Can we pay in USD?
faqs.answer: While the contract can state a USD amount, the local payout and tax withholdings MUST be calculated and paid in CLP to comply with local bank and tax regulations.

items.title: Liquidación de Sueldo
items.description: The monthly payslip detailing all gross earnings, discounts (social/tax), and net payment. Must be signed (physically or digitally) by the employee.

items.title: Libro de Remuneraciones Web
items.description: Companies with 5+ employees must upload their payroll book to the DT portal every month.

items.title: Previred Voucher
items.description: Proof of social security payment, critical for obtaining 'F30' compliance certificates.

steps.title: Gross Base Entry
steps.description: Input the base monthly salary in CLP, including any taxable 'Haberes' (Allowances).

steps.title: Statutory Deduction Subtracting
steps.description: Automatically deducting the ~10% AFP (Pension), 7% Health (Isapre/Fonasa), and 0.6% Unemployment (employee portion).

steps.title: Income Tax (IRPP) Application
steps.description: Applying the progressive tax brackets based on the current UTM value (Monthly Tax Unit).

steps.title: Non-Taxable Additions
steps.description: Adding 'Colación' (Meals) and 'Movilización' (Transport) stipends which are not subject to tax or social security.

steps.title: Employer Cost Consolidation
steps.description: Summing the SIS, Mutual (Accident insurance), and employer AFC portions to show the total 'Costo Empresa'.

items.title: The UTM Factor
items.text: Income tax is calculated in UTM. Because UTM changes monthly with inflation, the tax brackets shift slightly throughout the year.

items.title: Social Security Caps
items.text: Social security contributions are capped at a certain UF (Unidad de Fomento) amount (approx 84.3 UF). Salaries above this cap pay no more in AFP/Health.

items.title: Net-to-Gross Agreements
items.text: It is common in Chile for employees to negotiate in 'Neto' (Take-home). The calculator helps figure out the Gross salary required to meet that net target.

faqs.question: What is the current value of 1 UTM?
faqs.answer: As of early 2025, 1 UTM is approximately 66,200 CLP. This value is updated monthly by the SII.

faqs.question: Does the calculator handle 'Isapre' variable plans?
faqs.answer: The calculator uses the mandatory 7% minimum. Excess health costs (the 'Cotización Adicional') depend on the employee's private contract with their Isapre.

faqs.question: Are the bonuses included?
faqs.answer: Yes, our calculator includes a toggle for the 25% Legal Gratification (capped at 4.75 SMVM) to ensure total cost accuracy.

items.title: UF Rate Sync
items.description: Always check the current day's UF value for accurate capping of social security.

items.title: Minimum Wage Check
items.description: Ensure the planned salary is above the July 2025 net floor of 500,000 CLP.

items.title: Municipal Tax ID
items.description: Required for the company to correctly withhold and pay these taxes on behalf of the worker.

heroData.title: Entity Setup and Incorporation in Chile
heroData.subtitle: Fast-Track Business Formation in South America's Trade Hub
heroData.description: Establish your SpA or SRL in as little as 48 hours using the 'Tu Empresa en un Día' portal. We handle everything from drafting bylaws and obtaining your RUT (Tax ID) to opening compliant business bank accounts and setting up your registered office in Santiago.
heroData.bestFor: Enterprises seeking long-term ownership, local commercial operations, and access to Chile's extensive network of 30+ Free Trade Agreements.

steps.title: Bylaws Drafting and Notarization
steps.description: Defining the company name, capital, administration structure, and business purpose. For SpA (Sociedad por Acciones), this can be done via private document signature or through the 'Empresa en un Día' system.

steps.title: SII Tax ID (RUT) Registration
steps.description: Obtaining the 'Rol Único Tributario' from the Internal Revenue Service. This is required for all legal entities to operate, sign contracts, and pay taxes in Chile.

steps.title: Initiation of Activities (Inicio de Actividades)
steps.description: Formally notifying the SII that the company has begun commercial operations. This step requires a verified 'Domicilio' (legal address).

steps.title: Municipal License (Patente Municipal)
steps.description: Obtaining the permit to operate a business from the local municipality based on the office location. Fee is usually 0.5% of the initial capital annually.

steps.title: Bank Account Opening
steps.description: The most time-consuming step. Requires vetting of all shareholders/directors (KYC) and proof of the foreign parent company's existence if applicable.

items.title: SpA vs. SRL
items.text: The SpA (Corporation by Shares) is the most popular for startups and international firms as it allows for a single shareholder and easy transfer of shares. The SRL (Limited Liability) requires at least two partners.

items.title: Foreign Shareholder Representative
items.text: Foreign shareholders must appoint a local 'Representante Legal' who is a Chilean resident. They hold the ultimate responsibility for the company's local actions.

items.title: Capital Requirements
items.text: There is no statutory minimum capital, but 1,000,000 CLP is recommended for initial bank vetting. Capital must be declared and registered with the SII.

items.title: Free Trade Access
items.text: Incorporating in Chile grants access to one of the world's most open economies, with FTAs covering ~90% of global GDP, including the US, EU, and China.

faqs.question: Can a 100% foreign-owned entity open a bank account?
faqs.answer: Yes, but expect a 30-90 day lead time. Compliance and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) checks in Chile are extremely rigorous for international parents.

faqs.question: Do I need to be physically present to incorporate?
faqs.answer: No. With a valid Power of Attorney (POA) apostilled in your home country, a local lawyer can complete all steps up to and including RUT registration on your behalf.

faqs.question: What is the SME tax rate for 2025?
faqs.answer: The SME regime (Pro Pyme) enjoys a reduced First Category Tax rate of 12.5% for the 2024-2026 tax years. Large companies pay 27%.

faqs.question: Is a physical office required?
faqs.answer: For tax purposes, a 'Domicilio Tributario' is required. Virtual offices are legal and commonly used by service-based startups and international firms.

items.description: Specific authority granted to the local representative to sign deeds and represent the entity at the SII.

items.title: High-Demand Skillsets
items.text: Cloud architects (AWS/Azure), Data Scientists, Mining Engineers, and Bilingual Project Managers (English/Spanish) are currently at the top of the 'most wanted' list.

items.title: University Pedigree
items.text: Graduates from 'Pontificia Universidad Católica' and 'Universidad de Chile' are highly regarded. Consider these as primary talent hubs for executive roles.

items.title: Contractual Binding
items.text: In Chile, an offer letter is often legally followed by an employment contract within 15 days. Candidates are highly risk-aversive and value contract stability.

items.title: Remote vs. Hybrid Trends
items.text: While Santiago remains the hub, hybrid models are now standard for the tech sector. Offering work-from-home options is a key differentiator for talent attraction.

faqs.question: What is the typical time-to-hire in Chile?
faqs.answer: For mid-level roles, expect 4-6 weeks. Executive or highly technical roles may extend to 8-12 weeks due to multiple vetting stages.

faqs.question: Is English proficiency common?
faqs.answer: English proficiency is variable. It is high in the tech and international trade sectors, but for general administrative roles, Spanish is the dominant language.

faqs.question: How do you handle background checks?
faqs.answer: We use specialized services to check 'Certificado de Antecedentes' (Criminal record) and verify employment history. Credit checks (DICOM) are restricted for recruitment purposes.

faqs.question: Can you recruit for seasonal mining roles?
faqs.answer: Yes, we have specialized pipelines for the northern mining regions (Antofagasta, Calama) where mobilization and camp-life experience are required.

items.title: Non-Discrimination Laws
items.description: Chile has strict laws against discrimination by age, gender, or health status in job postings and interviews.

items.title: Data Protection (Law 19.628)
items.description: Candidate data must be handled with strict confidentiality and explicit consent for processing.

items.title: Foreign Labor Limit
items.description: Companies with 25+ employees must ensure at least 85% of their workforce are Chilean nationals, with some exceptions for technical roles.

items.title: Licencias Médicas (Sick Leave)

items.title: IFRS in Chile
items.text: Chile officially adopted IFRS in 2009. All large companies and most SMEs reporting to international parents must use full IFRS or IFRS for SMEs.

items.title: The 'DTE' System
items.text: Chile is a global leader in electronic invoicing (DTE). Every single business transaction must be logged digitally with the SII in real-time.

items.title: Audit Preparedness
items.text: Maintain clear 'Libros de Compra' and 'Libros de Venta' (Purchase/Sales books) in digital format. The SII can conduct remote audits with minimal notice.

items.title: UF and UTM Usage

faqs.question: What is the 'Declaración de Renta'?
faqs.answer: It is the annual income tax return (Form 22) filed in April for the preceding calendar year. It reconciles paid monthly taxes (PPMs) against final corporate profits.

faqs.question: What is 'PPM'?
faqs.answer: Pagos Provisionales Mensuales (Monthly Provisional Payments) are prepayments of corporate income tax. The rate is usually 1% - 2.5% of monthly gross sales.

faqs.question: Is external audit mandatory?
faqs.answer: For large corporations (SAs) and certain financial entities, it is mandatory. For private SpAs, it is usually requested by shareholders or banks for credit lines.

items.title: F29 (Monthly Tax)
items.description: Due by the 20th of every month (for electronic filers).

items.title: Annual Tax (April)
items.description: The 'Operation Renta' period where final corporate taxes are settled.

items.title: March Sworn Statements

steps.title: Internal Work Regulations drafting

steps.title: Statutory Records Archiving
steps.description: Maintaining physical and digital archives of all critical corporate documents (Bylaws, Shares, Minutes) available for audit.

items.title: The 'F30-1' Criticality
items.text: This certificate is required for participation in public tenders, subcontracting relationships, and obtaining bank credit. A single day of late social security payment voids this status.

items.title: Environmental Compliance (SMA)
items.text: Companies with industrial impact must report regularly to the 'Superintendencia del Medio Ambiente'. Fines for non-compliance are among the highest in Latin America.

items.title: Anti-Corruption (Law 20.393)
items.text: Chilean law holds corporations criminally liable for crimes committed by their representatives (bribery, money laundering). Implementing a 'Crime Prevention Model' is highly advised.

faqs.question: What is the 'RETC'?
faqs.answer: The Registro de Emisiones y Transferencia de Contaminantes (RETC) is a mandatory environmental reporting system for companies that generate specific types of waste or emissions.

faqs.question: Is insurance mandatory for all employees?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every employee must be covered by Law 16.744 against work accidents and professional diseases via a Mutual or the public ISL.

faqs.question: What happens if we lose our F30-1 status?
faqs.answer: Clients may withhold payments, and you will be barred from major contracts until the underlying labor/social debt is settled and the certificate is re-issued.

items.title: Integrated Tax System
items.text: Chile uses an integrated system where corporate tax paid (IDPC) can often be used as a credit against the final taxes of the shareholders.

items.title: General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR)
items.text: The SII has expanded powers to challenge transactions deemed to be solely for tax avoidance. Substance-over-form is the guiding principle.

items.title: SME Tax Holidays
items.text: Qualifying SMEs (Pro Pyme regime) currently enjoy a reduced 12.5% corporate tax rate, significantly lower than the standard 27% for large corps.

faqs.question: What is the VAT rate in Chile?
faqs.answer: The standard Value Added Tax (IVA) rate is 19%. It applies to most goods and services, including digital services provided by foreign entities to local individuals.

faqs.question: Does Chile have tax treaties with the US?
faqs.answer: Yes, the US-Chile Tax Treaty entered into force in late 2023, significantly reducing withholding taxes on interest, dividends, and royalties between the two countries.

faqs.question: Is profit remittance taxed?
faqs.answer: Dividends sent abroad are subject to a 35% Additional Tax, but the corporate tax paid locally (27%) can usually be used as a credit, resulting in an effective net tax of ~8% or 35% depending on treaty status.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Staffing and MSA in Chile?
faqs.answer: Staffing provides individuals (input-based), while MSA provides a complete service or project (outcome-based). MSA shifts the operational and labor management risk to the provider.

faqs.question: How do you handle the 40-hour week transitions in MSA?
faqs.answer: As the provider, we manage the staffing rosters and shifts to ensure SLA continuity despite the reduction in individual working hours, without increasing the client's base fee.

faqs.question: Are MSA contracts subject to VAT?
faqs.answer: Yes, as of 2023, most professional services in Chile are subject to 19% VAT (IVA). We ensure invoices are correctly issued as 'Factura de Ventas y Servicios'.

heroData.title: Software and IT Solutions for Chile
heroData.subtitle: Enabling Business Efficiency with Localized Platforms
heroData.description: Drive your digital transformation in Chile with software built for the local market. From best-in-class HR platforms like Buk and Rex+ to comprehensive SAP ERP localizations and modern API-first fintech solutions, we help you choose and implement the right stack for 2025.
heroData.bestFor: Enterprises needing localized ERP, HR, and Billing software that integrates directly with Chilean tax (SII) and labor (DT) systems.

steps.title: Local Compliance Mapping
steps.description: Identifying software that natively supports Chilean Electronic Invoicing (DTE), Previred file formats, and the 40-hour week logic.

steps.title: Integration with SII Portal
steps.description: Configuring 'Rest APIs' or standard connectors to sync sales and purchase invoices directly with the Servicio de Impuestos Internos.

steps.title: Data Residency and Privacy Setup
steps.description: Ensuring cloud infrastructure meets the evolving Chilean data protection standards (Law 19.628) and local banking security protocols.

steps.title: User Training in Spanish
steps.description: Executing adoption workshops for local teams, focusing on the nuances of Chilean business processes and reporting.

steps.title: Ongoing Hyper-care and Support
steps.description: Providing local-time support to manage the frequent annual updates in Chilean tax laws and labor directorate mandates.

items.title: The Dominance of SaaS
items.text: Chilean businesses have rapidly adopted SaaS. Local leaders like Buk (People Ops) have set a high bar for user experience and local compliance.

items.title: DTE Certification
items.text: Ensure any ERP or Billing software is an 'Emisor Autorizado' by the SII. Non-certified software requires a painful manual upload process.

items.title: Fintech Integration
items.text: Leverage Chile's advanced banking APIs (Transbank, Flow, Mercado Pago) for seamless e-commerce and B2B payment processing.

faqs.question: Can we use international ERPs like NetSuite in Chile?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they require a 'Chilean Localization' package to handle the specialized DTE (Electronic Invoicing) and local tax books required by the SII.

faqs.question: What is Buk?
faqs.answer: Buk is the leading HR management system in Chile. It is often preferred by international firms for its perfect alignment with Chilean labor law and user-friendly interface.

faqs.question: How do you handle data backups?
faqs.answer: All solutions we implement include automated daily backups with geo-redundancy (often in AWS Santiago or US-East regions) to ensure business continuity.

items.title: Entel/Movistar Connectivity
items.description: Reliable fiber-optic fiber is a prerequisite for Chilean SaaS operations.

items.title: SII Digital Token
items.description: Mandatory for authentication between your software and the tax authority.

items.title: Local 24/7 Service Desk
items.description: Support in Spanish to handle complex local configuration requests.

heroData.title: Marketing and PR Agencies in Chile
heroData.subtitle: Connecting Your Brand to the Chilean Consumer
heroData.description: Navigate the unique cultural and digital landscape of Chile. Our partner agencies in Santiago specialize in cross-border brand entry, localized SEO for the .cl domain, and high-impact influencer campaigns tailored to the Chilean 'Modismo' and consumer behavior.
heroData.bestFor: International brands looking to establish a localized presence and drive growth in South America's most stable economy.

steps.title: Chilean Consumer Deep-Dive
steps.description: Analyzing local purchasing habits, preferred social platforms (Instagram and TikTok are dominant), and the impact of the '.cl' domain on local trust.

steps.title: Brand Localization (Spanish-CL)
steps.description: Adapting messaging to include Chilean Spanish nuances (modismos) while maintaining a professional and reliable brand voice suitable for the local market.

steps.title: Influencer and PR Activation
steps.description: Partnering with local Santiago-based influencers and 'Journalists' to build rapid brand authority and social proof.

steps.title: Performance Marketing Launch
steps.description: Executing targeted Google Ads and Meta campaigns, optimized for the Chilean peak shopping seasons (CyberDay, Black Friday, and Fiestas Patrias).

steps.title: ROI Analytics and Scaling
steps.description: Monitoring conversion rates specifically for Chilean payment methods like Webpay and adjust spend for maximum efficiency.

items.title: The '.cl' Advantage
items.text: Chileans prefer shopping on .cl domains. Using a local domain significantly improves SEO rankings and click-through rates compared to .com.

items.title: CyberDays Impact
items.text: E-commerce events like CyberMonday (organized by the CCS) accounts for a massive portion of annual retail sales. Planning campaigns 3 months in advance is essential.

items.title: Consumer Rights (Sernac)
items.text: Chile has a very strong consumer protection agency (SERNAC). Misleading advertising or poor refund policies can lead to heavy fines and public 'funas' (shaming).

faqs.question: What are the top marketing agencies in Santiago?
faqs.answer: Sherlock Communications, INPULSE, and Adsformance are highly rated on Clutch for their digital strategy and local market execution.

faqs.question: Is Google or Meta more effective in Chile?
faqs.answer: Meta (Instagram/WhatsApp) is exceptionally powerful for B2C, while Google Search remains the leading choice for B2B and high-intent purchasing.

faqs.question: How important is WhatsApp in Chilean marketing?
faqs.answer: Crucial. Most small to medium-sized businesses use WhatsApp Business as their primary customer service and sales channel.

items.title: Local CASE Studies
items.description: Ensure the agency has successfully launched international brands in the Chilean market before.

items.title: Bilingual Account Managers
items.description: Essential for clear communication between HQ and the local execution team.

items.title: Webpay Integration Knowledge
items.description: The agency should understand the local checkout flow and how to optimize for it.
